Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383, at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the Council meetings; however, to allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to comment or make a presentation shall be limited to three (3) minutes. Anyone wishing to address the City Council is requested to fill out a green speakerâ€™s card available at the end of each row in the Chambers. DRAFT MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA
  November 13, 2012

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Palos Verdes Estates was called to order
this day at 7:00 PM in the Council Chambers of City Hall by Mayor Bird.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEM(S)

CLOSED SESSION (7:00 p.m. - 7:30 p.m.)

CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT

CA Hogin discussed item as agendized but took no reportable action.

CEREMONIAL MATTERS

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL (7:00 PM)

PRESENT:  Mayor Bird, Mayor Pro Tem Goodhart, Councilmember Humphrey,
  Councilmember Perkins, Councilmember Rea
ABSENT:  None

ALSO PRESENT:  Chief Eberhard, City Manager Smith, Public Works Director Rigg, City
  Treasurer Sherwood, City Attorney Hogin, Asst. to City Manager Davis,
  Asst./Deputy City Clerk Kroneberger

MAYOR'S REPORT - MATTERS OF COMMUNITY INTEREST

Marvin Jackmon, SCE, update on containment plan, outages, and new on the Peninsula. There are
12 areas where different to limit duration of outages when they odccur; last one completed
September 10 2012, started in April. All have been completed. Devices installed were under
budget; took leftover funds to do additional work in PVE (more devices) to address end of year
crunch; alot of work taking place on teh peninsula. The long term plan was contingent on teh
general rate case; proposed decision came out on October 19th; the process is not over due the
comnment period in November. A final decision is sexpected first of 2013. Then they will know
what funds can be expected to continue improvement of infrastructure on the Peninsula. Provided
graph from Januar 2011 to October 2012, there were quite a few outages. Containment plan
included time out as a factor; outages have dropped significantly since infrastructure improved.
Same period, there were 9 outages (30 for same period Jan-Oct 2011); 8 hours total outage. The
containment plan is working and has improved significantly. They are conducting cable
testingproactively to see hwo robust or bad they are; expecting preliminary reports for life of cables
CITY COUNCIL
November 13, 2012

  1
 and will input in their cable replacement program. Confirmed by C/M Smith that the cable testing
is done for underground cables to determine life expectancy; will provide results at next report. He
said he was excited about the number of outages and progress made.

MPT Goodhart complimented SCE for doing what they said would be done with the short term
plan. Power outage on PVDN recently 10:15 p.m. and on at 3:30 a.m. when water main burst.
Interesting comment received by businesses recently regarding outages; suffering economic
impacts. Through SCE assistance, damage to electronic equipment due to surges; helpful in getting
required claim forms, but SCE rejected the claims due to power outage caused damage. Cmbr
Perkins and he and number of residents testified before PUC; a common theme was conveyed
regarding lack of responsiveness, communication, advanced warning for power outage, Manhattan
Bch PD incurred traffic light outages. RPV concerned about Portugese Bend and fire in 2009
with powerlines and was concerned that it could happen here. The rate case - reduced budget by
over $800m which impacts long term plan and asked when it would be resolved.

Mr. Jackmon said they expect a final decision in January regarding the rate case; they will report
how this effects their long term plan. Net to rate will be impacted as well. some of the outages in
terms of claims, protecting equipment from rodents, weather, things that they do not have control
over regarding claims. MPT Goodhart said he hoped SCE focuses alot of the resources in this area
and offered help; he confirmed Mr. Jackmon would return when that information is available.

Councilember Perkins said she appreciated attention paid to the Peninsula and progress made.
Cable tested has provided great promise in being proactive to address issues such as unplanned
outages. She asked who decides when cables can be "go away" at the end of hte year; how is
planning for these funds done or where does that money go.

Mr. Jackmon said the good news from results of cable testing, results are placed into the
replacement program faster because it is determined sooner what must be replaced. The idea is to
move up timing iof replacement of cables. She asked if they will be able to spend all allocated
funds before the end of the year. They are working with the cities to work across their service area;
the key is to have the work orders ready to go. Short term plan had that detail and they're doing
quite a bit of work in the South Bay to get done by December 31st.

Mayor Bird thanks SCE for addressing the program regarding aging equipment and cable issues.
The containment plan status does not contemplate the 3-5 year budget. This is an effort by Edison
to be more proactive to addressing problems in PVE. Going forward, the planning for replacement
of equipment is planned continuously. Above and beyond the containment plan. He asked what
could be expected in the next 12 months. Mr. Jackmon said they will take results/capitol funds and
apply them to the long term plan. Only done if we pay more for electricity. GRC process assumes
a certain amount of funds, irregardless of rates.

Mayor Bird said they had criticized SCE becuase not being proactive enough. Consumer funds
weren't being allocated to replacement of equipment. Can they still expect SCE commitment to
replace aging infrasture in PVE; Jackmon said yes. Bird said only 8 hours outages, a benefit to our
residents, SCE has used to addressed our outages issues.

CITY COUNCIL
November 13, 2012

  2
 Councilmember Humphrey asked about electric reliability would be addressed in the City
newsletters. City Manager Smith said the information will be included in it.

Mayor Bird thanked Mr. Jackmon.

10 ft. No plans or permissions were given to approve the encroachments. Not addressed with
success. Gave his military and scholastic credentials and spoke of neighbors would like work on
Pima path and Alcance and wants help to bring use of path to all. Mayor Bird said they will look
into this issue and will get a report from city staff.

saving old elm trees v. removing them..tree v. view..replaced by magnolia trees; everyone happy
now. Enormous trees on private property; trees were reduced to the roof line. New residents have
planted gigantic palm trees along PDM - 15 counted; some on city property; some on private
property. Visited new resident with no response; another one has been planted since. Spoke
atParkland sCommittee and Mr. Rigg agreed alot of trees.

 Mayor Bird has jurisdiction on private trees on private proeprty; if on public property, it would be

She asked about the rule about planting trees above the roof line. Bird suggested he speak with
staff. Spoke of Item #8 regarding Ambassador Program to dsicuss unique issues regarding their

7.  Approval of Concession Agreement - Palos Verdes Golf Club

On motion of Rea, seconded by Perkins, Council approved Approval of Concession Agreement -
Palos Verdes Golf Club by unanimous oral vote.

AYES:  Bird, Goodhart, Humphrey, Perkins, Rea
NOES:  (None)
ABSTAIN: (None)
RECUSED: (None)
ABSENT: (None)

On motion of Rea, seconded by Perkins, Council approved Approval of Concession Agreement -
Palos Verdes Golf Club by unanimous oral vote.

AYES:  Bird, Goodhart, Humphrey, Perkins, Rea
NOES:  (None)
ABSTAIN: (None)
RECUSED: (None)
ABSENT: (None)

Mayor Bird recused because he is member of hte Golf Club; turned gavel over to MPT Goodhart.

City Manager Smith said PVGC is run under a concession agreement with City; 10/2010 most
recent; increase in member from 560 to 600 members; including members of non-residents to join
club. As a result of those changes; complete revision of bylaws has been completed. Council liaison
Perkins, Rea nd herself met with members of hte club and the GM in May and Septemer to review
proposed changes. A redline version was also provided to; mostly form over substance. Terms of
the agreement, exp. 12/31/2024 plus 4 five year options to extend. Budget, audito report, required
contributions - none of those provisions change. Membership provisions do not change either.
Addressed were definitions, including "regular" member and exhibits that show actual description
of the Club; updated insurance and indem process. Process also provided for distruction of
htepremises; cost of rebuilding, and standards for funding rebuilding. Use of premises and golf
course access to assure safety. Trail access was also discussed; they will partner with us as part of
CITY COUNCIL
November 13, 2012

  4
 trails enhancement process. Other membership categories included - inactive, waiting list, and
interpretation section addresses conflict - agreement prevails.

Councilember Rea thanked Mr. Hockett for cordial meetings; they were exntensive - significant
changes were made to clean up age old issues. It is a much better agreement now. He said
extensions could reach 2045, but reasonable considering the money spent to reburbish the Club
House. He was pleased to hear club will work with us with trail project and tying into trail systems
in our city.

Cmbr. perkins said this was a great opportunity; to provide City ATtorney op to take a look at this.
Surprised that maps were nto previously included, now memorialized. Use of premises
clarification was good for public safety and looking for future conversations regaridng public
access to the premises.

Cmbr Humphrey said she had been involved in years past in reitaretaions of hte agreement. She
thanked everyone involved in the many hours of work put into thsi very thorough review. Glad to
see attention to the pathways along the Club; exceleltn additon. No objections to the agreement.

MPT Goodhart thanked everyone involved. ASked about the term extensions Rea said a series of
extensions discussed; the construction had partly. 5 yr. increments will enable us to do that. he
asked if by-laws would return to Council. Rea said the club board can modify the bylaws; notify
the city to determine inconsistency..concession agreement controls it. They did not want GC
involved in writing the by-lows; this was a workable appraoch.

8.  Review and Approval of Proposed Outreach Program for New Homeowners – “City
  Ambassador Program”

On motion of Humphrey, seconded by Rea, Council approved Review and Approval of Proposed
Outreach Program for New Homeowners – “City Ambassador Program” by unanimous oral vote.

AYES:  Bird, Goodhart, Humphrey, Perkins, Rea
NOES:  (None)
ABSTAIN: (None)
RECUSED: (None)
ABSENT: (None)

Director Rigg said PVE is different; we have a variety of rules and processes. Often lead to
confusion, especially among newest residents. Frustrations regarding not knowing hte rules is dealt
with often. Most learn the rules once they are broken. Propose new outreach program to orient new
homeowners. Letters would be sent and they would be invited to part of process. Review of
address file which contains relevent documetns for every process in the City. Explain our City,
review the file, and specifc isues to their property. Staff could visit home to look at issues or
opportunities. Prime opportunity to educate as to the process if changes are appropriate.
Greatreturn will be realized for being proactive rather than gong through code enforcement.

Councilmember Rea asked whe property bought, e.g. disclosures such as lead paints, cC&Rs , but
CITY COUNCIL
November 13, 2012

  5
 not our city ordinances. He asked if City ordinance could be crafted that additional disclosures be
made, e.g. NC ordinance; are pre-empted by state law.

City Attorney Hogin said she did not think state law precludes, but wanted to think it through. She
suggested working with Homeowners association includes NC, and summaries of helpful rules.

MPT Goodhart said it is great idea because often times residents are unaware. starting now, going
forward...suggest we approach those that have purchased homes such as January 2010 going
forward; possibly help those that are closer to making that change.

Councilmember Perkins agreed that this is ag erat idea; education is better than resorting to
enforcement. Once residents are aware of this, residents will want to have access to the same kinds
of information.

Councilmember Rea said this is a great idea. On the PC, he said many were surprised to learn NC
existed. It should ultimately save time becauswe problems will be niped in the bud.

Councilmember Humphrey said this is a good idea; people move here because they like the
ambience of the City. One attractive thing is the look and she hoped that they are willing to be a
participant in maintaining what attracted them in the first place. Seh commended Director Rigg;
knowing what is permissible ahead of time is a great idea. She suported back tracking a little, such
as MPT Goodhart suggested. 35 homes sold/quarter - helping them understand policies and rules
to maintain what attracted them in the first place. it is a great program; article in City Newsletter
upon approval confirmed. Association of Realtors being approached? Director Rigg said they can
reach out to them..this program is similar to Peninsula Expert designation from board of Realtors to
expand their reach. She said real estate agents would want to have this program to share so nto to
run afoul with your neighbors. She thanks Director Rigg.

Mayor Bird asked when seminars presented. Association with Nancy Gunther..ABC's of the
Buidling process were presented about a year ago per City Manager Smith.

Mayor Bird said this ia proactive user friendly program to help our residents and future residents
who wish to buy proeprty here. Confusion regarding Homes Association processes and City
processes - goal is to approve plans that are inconformit wiht rules and regulations. This goes
along way and would hold off alot of problems; commende d Rigg.

9.  Review and Approval of Request for Proposal "Analysis of Service Delivery Options -
  Building, Planning, Public Works Administration"

On motion of Rea, seconded by Goodhart, Council approved Review and Approval of Request for
Proposal "Analysis of Service Delivery Options - Building, Planning, Public Works
Administration" by unanimous oral vote.

AYES:  Bird, Goodhart, Humphrey, Perkins, Rea
NOES:  (None)
ABSTAIN: (None)
CITY COUNCIL
November 13, 2012

  6
 RECUSED: (None)

City Manager Smith said this is October 9th Council determined more information on service
delivery options and requested RFP. Four different categories include; develop baseline
comparisons (current cost in-house), job duties and salary ranges, specific recommendation and
ratonale, and rec. associated with contract services hwo best to construct that contract. She said
reference made to Andersen study done in 1995; same scope and contact was done at that time.
CAA was contractor at that time; their recommendation was acombination in-house contract with
in-house dept. head. Projected cost savings weren't signfiicatn enough, per Council, to warrant
going in that direction. If approved, RFP would be dist immediatley; due December 14th; award in
January. Consultant would provide timeline for completion. RFP also provides for city selection
committee/interview. If so, she asked for two members from Council along with herself to conduct
interviews. No budget included for this process. Funded by General Fund unobligated balance if
CC wishes to proceed with RFP.

MPT Goodhart if to proceed, who would provide information city salary structure; provided by CM
and Asst to CM Davis; not a lot of staff time; info is readily available.

Cmbr. Humphrey asked if a month is long enought to get a good response. C/M Smith said 12/21
was the original response date. Electronic database available to post RFP. They are to prepare a
response to be considered for an award.

City ATtonrey Hogin said this isn't like a public works. They could extend it at their discretion;
there is flexibility provided to Council.

Cmbr. Rea said the 4 categories from 1995 RFP that results in Andersen hired? Generally, the
same scope..the tasks are the same. Rea confirmed that Andersen suggested it be brought back-
inhouse. ASk that the report be brought to Council. Question of bringing in house. City Manager
Smith said nature of work 18-20; diodn't know that any of the facotrs are still relevent today. Rea
said obscure regarding in-house. Smith said there could be a different arrangement suggested; such
as a planner in house or other. Bird said ti is good they have flexibility.

Speakers:

Brent Flynn, 601 VDM, 1995 Andersen report was reviewed and iin 2001 City did nto follow
recommendations of Andersen report; used other cities in their analysis. Conclusion said contract
engineering, poanning, with the exception of in-house currently held. Said they recomemnded it
would save oru city money; the lack of qualititative oversight quoted...quoted from study

eliminate current arrangement. This nontransprartent arrangement should end. Martin Oversier,
3657 Navajo Place, 12/14 due date - short response time to provide good proposal. Supported
extending it by an additional month.

Desire Myers, 1508 Via Lazo, alot of progress this year. core services agreed by cC for RFP,

 Andersen study resulted in benefits by in-housing engineer increase 7% savings/year. 2001 Council
chose not to make changes, which raises questions. Questioned time and material who decides
policy? quality, and other services. PVE remains only city that outsources..can accountability be
outsourced. Thanked CC for ..enumerated all accomplishments this past year.

MPT Goodhart said his experience in aerospace business; alot of assumptions for the proposal and
agreed with suggested extension for proposal due date to get a good quality proposal.

Perkins agreed. Sometimes qualified people will not respond and they wanted to do this well with
a good response to do an excellent analysis; supported extended antoehr month.

Rea asked if Andersen would be provided to ersondents. It is a public document, but we would like
fresh and unbiased approach and wouldn't want view tainted by what waas done previosuly. Smith
said this analyis was done 18 years ago; alot has changed but they would find out. He agreed 60

Bird said wouldnt' they want to see that report.

MPT said it could be offered.

Councilmeber humphrey said they should get a fresh look. Abbott was not on PVE City Council.
AGreed rfp for a good fresh look and maybe 12/14 is rushing it; perhaps some new good ideas
would be brought forth and provide them with information on how they might want to go forthl.

Bird said recommendation is... has heard consensus with favor of recommendaiton with due date of

C/M Smith sid they could make it available to successful proposed. Bird supported committee to
